findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the STATUS-event discriminator's value vocabulary (bool vs enum) and state which value each close path writes — gate-off, --force, config-unreadable, local-source, certifiable-false, expected-and-signed, expected-but-signature-lost — so AC2's three-way and AC3's not-gate-off distinctions are mechanically derivable from reduced state.
evidence: Direction: 'Record the EXPECTATION and its outcome on the close STATUS event' / 'an event-schema addition: field on the STATUS event'
AC2: 'distinguishes closed-and-signed from closed-with-signature-lost from closed-with-gate-off'
AC3: 'The --force, local-source, and certifiable-false closes are not reported as gate-off'

Problem lists six paths that collapse into one indistinguishable state (gate off, --force, config-unreadable-fails-open, local-source, certifiable-false, dropped sidecar) — a single boolean cannot separate these
findings.finding: The Direction specifies recording 'the EXPECTATION and its outcome' as 'a field on the STATUS event' (singular), but the acceptance criteria demand a multi-way discriminator that a single boolean cannot express: AC2 must separate signed / signature-lost / gate-off, and AC3 additionally requires --force, local-source, and certifiable-false closes to NOT read as gate-off. Since all of gate-off, force, local-source, certifiable-false, and dropped-sidecar currently collapse into 'closed with no attestation', a boolean 'was a signature expected' distinguishes gate-off from the rest but leaves force/local/certifiable-false indistinguishable from a genuine signature-lost close. The plan does not enumerate the field's value vocabulary (bool vs enum, and which value each of the six enumerated close paths writes).
findings.location: Direction paragraph ('Record the EXPECTATION and its outcome ... field on the STATUS event') vs Acceptance criteria AC2/AC3
scenarios: Executor picks a boolean expected-flag and AC3's force/local/certifiable-false cases are still indistinguishable from signature-lost
Reader cannot tell a withheld (certifiable-false) close from a lost-signature close
findings.suggested_fix: Define an enum-valued field (e.g. `completion_expectation` with values like `not_required`, `forced`, `local_unattested`, `withheld`, `required`) plus reader logic that treats `required` + missing attestation as signature-lost; state the config-unreadable-fails-open case's value explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the close-expectation is computed independently of verified_result (gate resolved on AND not an idea-reject close) and threaded into transition_core as a NEW consumed parameter, with a test asserting the value actually lands on the STATUS event (not silently dropped like force_close_reason).
evidence: _completion_precheck returns None for gate-off, --force, local-source, and certifiable-false alike (close_precheck.py:418,420,587,599) — so 'expected' cannot be inferred from its return value
transition_close.py:377-388 calls transition_core AFTER the precheck; the expectation is known outside the lock and must be passed in
Plan itself notes 'txn.transition_core accepts force_close_reason and never uses it — the parameter at _commands/txn.py:198 occurs exactly once and is silently discarded'
Direction names transition_core as the write point but does not describe computing/threading the expectation signal
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the 'a completion signature was expected' value is computed and threaded into transition_core; it is NOT the same as the precheck's verified_result (which is None for a --force close even though a signature was expected), and transition_core currently accepts force_close_reason yet silently discards it — so a naively-threaded expectation param risks being ignored or mis-derived.
scenarios: A --force close where the gate is ON: a signature WAS expected but the verifier was skipped and verified_result is None

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether the recorded expectation distinguishes config-unreadable (gate_enabled fail-open) from genuine gate-off, or acknowledge in the Problem/AC that this pair stays intentionally conflated.
evidence: Problem lists 'config unreadable -> gate_enabled fails OPEN (_commands/gates.py:79-87)' among the six states collapsed into one
gates.py:81-87 returns False on ConfigError (fail-open), the same value a genuinely-off gate yields
AC #3 enumerates --force, local-source, certifiable-false but does not name config-unreadable
Direction: 'gate-off reads as not-expected' — but a fail-open config-unreadable also reads as not-expected
findings.finding: The recorded 'expectation' derives from gate_enabled(), which fails OPEN (returns False) on unreadable config, so a config-unreadable close records 'not expected' and remains indistinguishable from a genuine gate-off close — a state the Problem section explicitly lists as collapsed but the solution does not resolve.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the close STATUS event records only the EXPECTATION (knowable at close-commit time) and that the OUTCOME is derived by the reader by diffing expectation against attestation presence in reduced state — or, if an outcome is genuinely stored, specify how signature-persistence result is known synchronously within the same locked write.
evidence: Direction sentence 1: 'Record the EXPECTATION and its outcome on the close STATUS event'
Direction sentence 3: 'A reader then compares "a completion signature was expected" against "a valid completion attestation exists"' — implies outcome is derived, not stored
Problem: the signature append is a distinct write whose failure is the bug — its result is not synchronously known at close-commit time
findings.finding: The Direction phrase 'record the EXPECTATION and its OUTCOME ... in the SAME locked write as the STATUS event' is ambiguous about the outcome's provenance/timing. The Premise establishes that the completion signature (attestation append) is a SEPARATE write that can fail AFTER the close commits — that is the entire bug. If 'outcome' means the signature-persistence result, it is not knowable at STATUS-write time. The reader-model sentence ('compares a completion signature was expected against a valid completion attestation exists') implies STATUS stores only the EXPECTATION and the reader DERIVES the outcome by diffing against attestation state — but the AC/Direction wording of 'record ... its outcome' contradicts that, leaving the executor unsure whether the STATUS event stores an outcome at all.
findings.location: Direction paragraphs ('Record the EXPECTATION and its outcome' vs 'compares ... expected against ... attestation exists')
scenarios: Executor tries to write signature-success into the STATUS event but the signature append happens later, so the value is always unknown or stale
findings.suggested_fix: State: STATUS stores expectation only; reader computes signature-lost = (expected == required) AND (no valid completion-verifier attestation in reduced state).
